subject: Pricing sensitivity & reserved GPU lanes — post-call recap
messages:
From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@aperturelabs.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-01T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Pricing sensitivity & reserved GPU lanes — post-call recap

Evelyn — thanks again for a productive call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have alignment.

Call highlights (from Aperture notes + our side):
- Expected steady-state inference: ~1.2B tokens/month (burst to 3B during peak launches).
- Primary workload: multi-turn clinical-retrieval assistant, average generated length ~120 tokens, average request tokens ~60.
- SLO: p95 latency <200ms on short prompts (~512 tokens context), tolerance for slightly higher on long context runs.
- Target economics: Aperture asked for a target unit goal in the $/1M tokens ballpark to justify reserved spend. You mentioned an internal budget range of $8k–$25k / 1M tokens depending on SLA and feature support.

Dedicated sizing thoughts (initial):
- GPU candidates: H100 80GB (best perf, higher cost) vs A100 80GB (good perf/cost balance).
- Reservation band: 4–12 GPUs initially — aimed at 1.2B steady tokens/month with headroom for bursts.
- Throughput target: ~40–90 tokens/sec sustained per GPU depending on batching/kv-cache efficacy; cluster-level goal ~3k–7k tokens/sec to hit peak.

Unit economics we ran live during the call (rough):
- If we provision 8 x A100 80GB with batching and prefix caching, estimated delivered cost ~ $10k–$14k per 1M tokens (includes infra + amortized SW/runtime).
- H100 flips that range up ~15–25% in cost but reduces p95 latency and increases tokens/sec per GPU.

Open items / asks for Aperture:
1) Confirm the budget band you can commit to for a 6–12 month reserved contract (helps us pick a GPU band and discount tier).
2) Share a 1-week sample traffic CSV showing request frequency and typical prompt+response token distribution (we can use anonymized data).
3) Prioritization: are latency p95 targets (short prompts) more important than absolute $/1M tokens?

Proposed next steps / timeline:
- I will circulate a formal pricing matrix (A100/H100, 4/8/12 GPU bands) with per-1M token unit economics and example throughput in a spreadsheet by EOD Tue (attached).
- If Aperture is comfortable, we propose a 4-week POC: 2 x A100 (dedicated) to validate throughput and caching assumptions; we’ll run benchmarks and share results.
- Procurement signal: if you can confirm a preliminary budget band and a decision window (e.g., by Oct 20), we’ll reserve capacity planning.

Thanks again — looping Marissa for the pricing matrix and Ben for any contract/req items.

Best,
Connor
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: aperture-pricing-matrix-v1.xlsx (will follow), poc-throughput-benchmark.pdf (ops notes)
From: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@aperturelabs.ai>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Aperture Labs Procurement <procurement@aperturelabs.ai>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-02T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & reserved GPU lanes — post-call recap

Connor — great summary, thanks. A few clarifications from our end: 
- The $8k–$25k / 1M tokens band I quoted is a hard internal target range; $8k would require significant latency compromises and model changes. Realistically procurement will be comfortable with $12k–$18k / 1M tokens if SLA and security items are satisfied.
- Decision timeline: we are aiming for a preferred vendor decision by Oct 22, target contract signature by Nov 12 (subject to procurement legal redlines).
- For the POC: we can provide a 7-day anonymized traffic dump. I’ll ask engineering to anonymize user ids but keep request/response token counts and timestamps intact.

Two questions: 1) For the initial POC footprint, would 2 x A100 be sufficient to validate burst handling under our sample traffic, or do you want to run an additional synthetic peak test? 2) Can you confirm whether Redwoods’ reserved pricing tiers include priority capacity during regional outages (i.e., fallback guarantees)?

I’m looping Procurement directly so they can be in the thread for budget/contract details.

Thanks,
Evelyn
Head of Product, Aperture Labs
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Park <evelyn.park@aperturelabs.ai>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-03T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & reserved GPU lanes — post-call recap

Evelyn — quick answers inline and attached is the first-pass matrix. See attachment: aperture-pricing-matrix-v1.xlsx

Q1 (POC footprint): 2 x A100 is usually sufficient to validate correctness and caching benefits on production traffic. For realistic peak simulation we recommend a short synthetic stress run (we can run from our side) that spikes to ~3x baseline to exercise autoscaling and fallback. If you'd like, we can include that as part of the 4-week POC scope.

Q2 (priority capacity / regional outage behavior): Reserved contracts include capacity reservation and a tiered fallback policy. Short version: we guarantee reserved capacity during normal operations; during large-scale regional outages we provide automatic cross-region failover to compatible model variants and prioritized scheduling for reserved tenants. Specific SLA exceptions and credits will be spelled out in the contract addendum — Ben, can you flag the standard reserved contract language and the outage credit table?

Pricing matrix notes (high level):
- 4 x A100: entry reserved band. Estimated delivered cost ~ $16k / 1M tokens (no deep prefix cache applied).
- 8 x A100: balanced delivery; estimated $11k–$13.5k / 1M tokens after expected batching and cache improvements.
- 8 x H100: estimated $13k–$16k / 1M tokens (better latency, higher sustained throughput).
- 12+ GPUs: discounted tiering available for 6–12 month commits (we’ll show exact numbers in the attached sheet).

Next steps: Connor will schedule a short POC kickoff; we’ll share the synthetic stress plan and updated pricing matrix with a decision checklist for procurement.

—Marissa
Sr. Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Aperture Labs Procurement <procurement@aperturelabs.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sensitivity & reserved GPU lanes — post-call recap

Hi Evelyn / Procurement team — thanks for the timeline. Attaching the contract summary and the reserved-capacity SLA excerpt (see attachment). A couple quick clarifications from legal/sales ops perspective: 
- Discounting: a 12-month commit at the 8-GPU band will unlock an additional 7% discount vs month-to-month reserved commitments.
- Outage credits: we provide service credits based on minutes of unplanned degraded reserved capacity; complete regional blackout scenarios have a separate escalation/credit table — we’ll include that in the draft.
- Procurement checklist: we need the following to speed to signature: 1) approved budget band (e.g., $12k–$16k / 1M tokens), 2) POC Statement of Work approval, 3) redlines to standard MSA if any.

Action: Connor to send POC SOW and calendar invite. Marissa to share final pricing sheet reflecting the budget band of $12k–$16k / 1M tokens.

Ben Carter
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments: reserved-contract-summary.pdf, aperture-pricing-matrix-v1.xlsx, poc-throughput-benchmark.pdf
